summary: This Thermostat class decides whether the system should be heating, cooling, or idle based on the current temperature and whether eco mode is on. A new printStatusToDisplay method sends that status to the console.

lines.text: The temperature reading is stored as final, so once a Thermostat is built its state cannot change; this makes the object predictable to test.
Eco mode is a simple on/off flag that widens the comfortable range, which is why the class has two behaviours to test rather than one.
The constructor takes both values up front, so every test can create a thermostat in exactly the situation it wants to check.
The this. prefix distinguishes the field from the constructor parameter of the same name.
Returning a String instead of printing is what makes this method easy to test: a test can compare the returned value against what it expects.
The conditional operator picks 65 when ecoMode is true and 68 otherwise, giving eco mode a lower point at which heating kicks in.
Eco mode also tolerates more heat before cooling starts, so the two thresholds together create a wider idle band.
Cold temperatures are handled first, and the early return means the later checks only run when this one does not apply.
The strict greater-than means a temperature sitting exactly on the cooling threshold counts as comfortable, not too hot.
Anything that falls through both checks is between the thresholds, so no action is needed.
This method is void because its whole job is a side effect: showing text on the display rather than handing a value back.
Reusing getStatus keeps the decision logic in one place, so the printed message can never disagree with the tested method.
